title: States and Union Territories of India - Administrative and Banking Network
content: Our service and banking platform operates across all 28 States and 8 Union Territories in India. The states covered include Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Odisha, Punjab, Rajasthan, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and West Bengal. The Union Territories include Delhi (National Capital Territory), Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Lakshadweep, and Puducherry. Customer complaints, accounts, and service requests can be registered from any state, city, district, or rural postal circle across the country with full multi-lingual support in English, Hindi, and regional languages including Odia.

title: Odisha State - Major Cities, Districts, and Operational Hubs
content: Odisha (state capital: Bhubaneswar, smart city code 751001-751030) is the primary operating circle for our regional support center. Key cities and district headquarters in Odisha include: Bhubaneswar (Saheed Nagar, Patia, Nayapalli, Khandagiri, Chandrasekharpur, Rasulgarh, Old Town), Cuttack (Badambadi, CDA, Choudwar, Link Road), Rourkela (Panposh, Civil Township, Koel Nagar), Berhampur (Ganjam district), Sambalpur (Western Odisha hub, Burla, Hirakud), Puri (Grand Road, Sea Beach), Balasore (Remuna, Chandipur road), Bhadrak (Charampa, Bonth), Kendrapara, Baripada (Mayurbhanj), Angul, Dhenkanal, Jharsuguda, Bargarh, Jeypore, Koraput, Rayagada, Jagatsinghpur, Paradeep, and Khordha (Jatani). Callers from Odisha can lodge service tickets and track orders across all 30 districts with native Odia language IVR assistance.

title: Eastern India - West Bengal, Bihar, and Jharkhand Cities
content: The Eastern Zone covers West Bengal, Bihar, and Jharkhand. In West Bengal, key service cities include Kolkata (state capital, Salt Lake, New Town, Park Street, Howrah), Asansol, Durgapur, Siliguri, Bardhaman, Kharagpur, and Haldia. In Bihar, major cities include Patna (state capital, Kankarbagh, Boring Road, Bailey Road), Gaya, Muzaffarpur, Bhagalpur, Darbhanga, Purnia, Begusarai, and Ara. In Jharkhand, primary industrial and banking centers include Ranchi (state capital, Doranda, Harmu), Jamshedpur (Tatanagar, Bistupur, Sakchi), Dhanbad, Bokaro Steel City, Deoghar, and Hazaribagh. Customers in these cities enjoy next-day door-step document verification and express replacement.

title: Northern India - Delhi NCR, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, and Haryana Cities
content: The Northern Region encompasses Delhi NCR, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, and Himachal Pradesh. In Delhi NCR, coverage includes New Delhi (Connaught Place, South Extension, Dwarka, Rohini), Noida, Greater Noida, Gurugram (Gurgaon, Cyber City, Golf Course Road), Faridabad, and Ghaziabad. In Uttar Pradesh, major hubs are Lucknow (capital, Hazratganj, Gomti Nagar), Kanpur, Varanasi, Agra, Prayagraj (Allahabad), Meerut, Bareilly, Aligarh, and Moradabad. In Punjab and Haryana, service hubs include Chandigarh (capital), Ludhiana, Amritsar, Jalandhar, Patiala, Panchkula, Panipat, Karnal, and Ambala. In Rajasthan, cities include Jaipur (Pink City capital, Malviya Nagar, Vaishali Nagar), Jodhpur, Udaipur, Kota, and Bikaner. In Uttarakhand, hubs include Dehradun and Haridwar.

title: Western India - Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Goa Cities
content: The Western Zone features major financial centers in Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Goa. In Maharashtra, key cities include Mumbai (financial capital, Nariman Point, Bandra-Kurla Complex BKC, Andheri, Borivali), Pune (Hinjawadi, Shivaji Nagar, Kothrud, Viman Nagar), Nagpur, Nashik, Thane, Navi Mumbai (Vashi, Belapur), Aurangabad (Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar), Solapur, and Kolhapur. In Gujarat, major business centers include Ahmedabad (SG Highway, Maninagar, Navrangpura), Surat (diamond and textile hub), Vadodara (Baroda), Rajkot, Gandhinagar (state capital), Bhavnagar, and Jamnagar. In Goa, service centers operate in Panaji (capital) and Margao.

title: Southern India - Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala
content: The Southern Region includes major technology and commercial capitals. In Karnataka: Bengaluru (Bangalore, Whitefield, Koramangala, Indiranagar, Electronic City, HSR Layout), Mysuru (Mysore), Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru, and Belagavi. In Telangana: Hyderabad (capital, Hitec City, Gachibowli, Banjara Hills, Secunderabad) and Warangal. In Andhra Pradesh: Visakhapatnam (Vizag), Vijayawada, Guntur, Tirupati, Nellore, and Kurnool. In Tamil Nadu: Chennai (capital, Anna Nagar, T. Nagar, OMR IT corridor, Guindy), Coimbatore, Madurai, Tiruchirappalli (Trichy), and Salem. In Kerala: Thiruvananthapuram (Trivandrum), Kochi (Cochin, Ernakulam, Kakkanad InfoPark), Kozhikode (Calicut), and Thrissur.

title: Central India - Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh Cities
content: The Central Region covers Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh. In Madhya Pradesh, major banking and service cities include Bhopal (state capital, MP Nagar, Arera Colony), Indore (commercial hub, Vijay Nagar, Palasia), Gwalior, Jabalpur, Ujjain, and Sagar. In Chhattisgarh, primary industrial and administrative centers include Raipur (state capital, Pandri, Telibandha), Bilaspur, Durg, Bhilai (Steel City), and Korba. Customer requests from these regions are processed with standard 3 to 5 business day SLAs.

title: North Eastern States of India - Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Regional Hubs
content: The North Eastern Region comprises the eight sister states: Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, and Tripura. Key administrative and service centers include Guwahati (Assam commercial gateway, Dispur capital, Paltan Bazaar, GS Road), Dibrugarh, Silchar, Jorhat, Tezpur, Shillong (Meghalaya capital), Agartala (Tripura capital), Imphal (Manipur capital), Aizawl (Mizoram capital), Kohima and Dimapur (Nagaland), Gangtok (Sikkim capital), and Itanagar (Arunachal Pradesh capital). All standard banking and grievance channels operate with full PIN-code coverage across North Eastern circles.

title: Indian Postal Pin Code Zones and Address Verification Policy
content: Postal Index Numbers (PIN codes) in India consist of 6 digits divided into 9 postal zones: Zone 1 (Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Chandigarh), Zone 2 (Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand), Zone 3 (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Daman and Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli), Zone 4 (Maharashtra, Goa, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh), Zone 5 (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka), Zone 6 (Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Puducherry), Zone 7 (West Bengal, Odisha, Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Meghalaya, Assam, Sikkim), Zone 8 (Bihar, Jharkhand), and Zone 9 (Army Post Office). Odisha PIN codes start with 75 or 76, West Bengal with 70 to 74, Bihar and Jharkhand with 80 to 85, Delhi with 11, Maharashtra with 40 to 44, and Karnataka with 56 to 59. When registering customer complaints or updating KYC address details, stating city, state, or PIN code ensures precise dispatch and field technician routing.

title: State-wise Customer Grievance and Support Jurisdiction
content: Customer support requests and registered complaints are automatically mapped to regional nodal grievance centers based on the caller's state and city: Eastern Circle (Bhubaneswar, Cuttack, Kolkata, Patna, Ranchi), Northern Circle (New Delhi, Lucknow, Jaipur, Chandigarh), Western Circle (Mumbai, Pune, Ahmedabad), Southern Circle (Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Kochi), and Central Circle (Bhopal, Raipur). If a caller is traveling or residing in another state, their registered complaint remains accessible across all circles nationwide, and tracking by complaint ticket number (e.g. 1, 15, CMP 0015) is universally synchronized.
